Overview

Lyon as a Business Centre

Lyon is France's second economic hub after Paris. The Métropole de Lyon, which groups 58 municipalities, has about 1.4 million residents, more than 175,000 businesses and nearly 650,000 private-sector jobs, and the wider metropolitan area exceeds 2.2 million people. Its economic base is industrial as much as tertiary: chemicals along the southern valley, life sciences and pharmaceuticals, food, textiles, banking and software, including a notable video games sector. The Part-Dieu district, described as France's second-largest tertiary district after La Défense, hosts regional banking, consulting and insurance offices, and the city is home to Interpol's headquarters and the International Agency for Research on Cancer.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Lyon because the region combines large multinational sites with a dense layer of mid-sized, often family-controlled industrial companies and suppliers. Buyers and investors need to understand who owns and runs those companies, how they are financed and whether they have litigation or insolvency history. Life sciences and chemicals groups face questions about distributors, contract manufacturers and departing employees with technical know-how. Lyon's court for economic activities handles a broad range of commercial and insolvency matters, so counsel frequently need well-sourced facts about counterparties, related companies and assets before or during proceedings.

Investigative Work Connected to Lyon

Life sciences partner and distributor diligence

Background research on contract manufacturers, distributors and licensing partners connected to Lyon's pharmaceutical, vaccine and diagnostics cluster, covering ownership, management, regulatory history, litigation and reputation, so that clients understand who they are relying on for quality-critical products and data.

02

Mid-sized family group ownership research

Mapping the holding structures, directors and financial filings of family-controlled industrial companies across the Lyon region, where control often sits in personal holding companies and related entities, to support acquisitions, minority investments and credit decisions.

03

Abrupt termination and supplier disputes

Factual support for counsel in disputes over the termination of established commercial relationships and supplier conflicts heard in Lyon, including research into the parties' trading history, related companies, public filings and prior proceedings relevant to damages and enforcement.

04

Insolvency and creditor research

Research for creditors, buyers and insolvency professionals on companies in safeguard, receivership or liquidation proceedings before Lyon's economic court, including management histories, transfers of assets to related entities and the background of prospective acquirers of distressed businesses.

Supporting counsel where engineers or researchers leave Lyon chemicals, life sciences or software employers for competitors or new ventures, through lawful research into the new businesses, their founders and their commercial activity, without covert methods or access to personal communications.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Lyon

Lyon economic activities court

Since 1 January 2025 the former Tribunal de commerce de Lyon has operated as a Tribunal des activités économiques (TAE), one of twelve pilot courts in a national experiment. Besides traditional commercial disputes, it can hear certain disputes involving liberal professions and farmers, and handles prevention and collective insolvency proceedings for debtors such as associations, civil companies and farms with registered offices in its area. Lyon also hears specialised disputes on abrupt termination of established commercial relationships.

Court registry and company records

The registry (greffe) of the Lyon commercial court keeps the trade and companies register (RCS) for businesses in its area, with filings available nationally through the Infogreffe service. Company extracts, statutes, director appointments and, where not kept confidential, annual accounts form the starting point for counterparty research. Insolvency judgments are also published, giving a public record of proceedings involving Lyon companies and their managers.

Arbitration and mediation in Lyon

The Lyon Métropole Chamber of Commerce and Industry has launched an arbitration and mediation chamber intended to offer businesses a simplified route for resolving commercial disputes locally. Larger international arbitrations involving Lyon companies are frequently seated in Paris or abroad. In any arbitration, investigative support is limited to factual research for counsel and the parties.

Higher courts in Lyon

Lyon is the seat of a cour d'appel, which hears appeals from the economic court and from the tribunal judiciaire de Lyon, the general first-instance court for civil matters and for criminal cases including economic and financial offences prosecuted locally. Identifying which Lyon court has handled a counterparty's disputes helps reconstruct its litigation history and any enforcement against it.

International organisations in the city

Interpol's General Secretariat and the International Agency for Research on Cancer are based in Lyon. Their presence does not create any special access to information: TDSC does not use police channels or non-public law enforcement data, and research relies on lawfully available public, commercial and court sources.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Lyon

For matters touching Lyon, TDSC begins by defining the commercial question, such as who controls a regional supplier, whether a distressed company's assets have moved to related entities, or what a former employee's new venture is doing. Research is conducted from Nashville using the trade and companies register, published insolvency and court information, French-language press and specialised trade sources. Where document retrieval, site visits or interviews are justified, TDSC coordinates with appropriately authorised French professionals and the client's counsel rather than acting directly. Personal data is handled under the GDPR with a defined purpose and minimised collection, and findings are presented in a form counsel can use before Lyon courts or arbitral tribunals.

TDSC has no office in Lyon. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Lyon: Frequently Asked Questions

What changed at the Lyon commercial court in 2025?

From 1 January 2025 it became a Tribunal des activités économiques as part of a national pilot. Its remit widened to certain disputes involving liberal professions and farmers, and to insolvency proceedings for debtors such as associations and civil companies. For research purposes this means more insolvency records for non-commercial entities in the Lyon area now sit with one court.

Can you identify who really owns a family-controlled company near Lyon?

Register filings usually show directors and the immediate shareholders, which may be personal holding companies. We trace those holdings through further filings, published accounts and press coverage to build a picture of control. Access to the French beneficial ownership register has been restricted, so we explain clearly where ownership is documented and where it is inferred.

Can you help in an abrupt termination of commercial relationship dispute?

We support counsel by researching the parties' trading history, corporate relationships, financial position and prior litigation, using lawful public and commercial sources. The legal analysis of the relationship and of damages remains with French counsel; our role is to provide accurate, sourced facts that help them build or test the case.

Does Interpol being in Lyon help investigations?

No. Interpol is an intergovernmental police organisation and its channels are for law enforcement. TDSC does not have, seek or imply access to Interpol notices beyond what is publicly published, nor to any police database. Our research uses public records, commercial data, court information and open sources gathered lawfully.

Does TDSC have an office in Lyon?

No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office or staff in Lyon or elsewhere in France. Most work is desk-based research. Where local steps are needed, we coordinate with appropriately authorised French professionals and the client's counsel, and we decline requests involving pretexting, covert recording or access to restricted records.
